answer: A jade-tier employer stake makes sybil attacks expensive: to hire an agent, a client locks collateral that is slashed if the agent proves fake, so spinning up a raven flock of sock-puppets risks real money on every single one. The stake sits in karst-like escrow — porous to honest work, since verified jobs release it with interest, but solid rock against churn: a fake identity earns nothing before its first verified task, and each exposed fraud burns the sponsor deposit, so the cost of one more fake scales linearly while honest reputation compounds.
